subject.title: [Feature]: Pattern-based channel allowlist for Discord (glob/wildcard support)

question: Should Discord channel access support a bounded glob-pattern form, and if so what precedence should it have relative to exact ids/names/slugs, thread-parent matches, and literal `*`?
rationale: This changes the inbound authorization boundary, and source evidence does not establish a safe existing public pattern contract or a mechanically implied precedence.

options.title: Approve a bounded Discord glob contract
options.body: Define a documented non-regex pattern grammar with exact and parent matches taking precedence over patterns, and patterns taking precedence over the literal `*` fallback.

options.title: Prefer category configuration
options.body: Resolve the dynamic-channel workflow through the category-level design tracked at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/60582 instead of adding name-based matching.

options.title: Retain exact allowlists
options.body: Keep the current explicit channel allowlist model if the authorization broadening and naming volatility are not acceptable.

recommendation.title: Approve a bounded Discord glob contract
recommendation.body: Define a documented non-regex pattern grammar with exact and parent matches taking precedence over patterns, and patterns taking precedence over the literal `*` fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared matcher and its existing fallback precedence are the central decision surface.
